target_customer: Venezuelan migrants in Colombia and people and small businesses in Latin America exposed to depreciating currencies
problem: People in hyperinflationary Latin American economies had trouble holding and moving dollars. Valiu offered a synthetic dollar savings wallet backed by Bitcoin and cross-border remittances from Colombia to Venezuela.
business_model: Remittance and FX spread fees plus a dollar savings wallet
product_category: Crypto backed dollar wallet and remittances

founders.name: Simon Chamorro
founders.background_notes: YC page and Forbes Colombia identify him as co-founder and CEO. Now a partner at Alliance per YC page.

founders.name: David Barinas
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says product hacker.

exit.reason: The CEO said the company did not adapt fast enough as Venezuela dollarized, the pandemic hit and crypto adoption grew; users were told to withdraw funds by Dec 15 and pointed to Reserve.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile wallet, remittance rails and a synthetic dollar backed by Bitcoin, with compliance and liquidity partners across two countries.

defensibility.rationale: Remittance corridors and stablecoin wallets were easy for others to replicate, and the Venezuelan market shifted to dollars and other platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Valiu told users to move to Reserve when it closed in December 2021. Airtm later received a $15M investment from the Stellar foundation in May 2021, per The Block.

market_need_then: Venezuelan hyperinflation and mass emigration to Colombia created demand for dollar savings and remittances, per the YC description and press coverage.

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage in Spanish language and crypto outlets across the funding and shutdown, and more than 30,000 users reported at closure

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in LatAm crypto and fintech press and reached about 30,000 users, but no mascot or community ritual and the product never found durable fit.

pivots.to: Synthetic dollar savings wallet (USDv) and broader LatAm dollar banking
pivots.why: Early 2020 launch of USDv to let users protect savings from depreciation, per Decrypt and Contxto coverage

outcome_analysis: Valiu began with Colombia to Venezuela remittances, added a Bitcoin backed synthetic dollar in 2020 and announced a 5.25 million dollar seed round led by Blockchange and Pomp. It grew to more than 30 staff and 30,000 users but closed in December 2021. The CEO blamed Venezuela dollarizing, the pandemic and faster crypto adoption, while former employees told Forbes it never found product market fit and chased too many products. The failure factors reflect those statements.
notes: The seed was reported 2020-12-08 by FinTech Global and 2021-02-11 by The Block; I used December 2020 and flagged the conflict. The Block states a $20 million valuation but not whether it is pre or post money, so post_money is null. Total raised per Forbes is more than $5M; CB Insights lists $6.64M over four rounds, Seedtable lists a $1.3M estimated seed in 2020, and the 2019-09 $1.227M round rests on Alphagrowth alone (single database). Search summaries named Alberto Niego as a co-founder but I did not open a source that says so, so he is not listed. Competitors: no dated 2019 source was opened (Airtm funding news is from 2021), so none are listed; Airtm, Reserve and Bitso were active in the region. Website returned empty content. Dates of the closure come from Forbes Colombia (2021-12-21).
